claim: Roncalli and Weisang (Risk Parity Portfolios with Risk Factors, MPRA 44017, 2012): the Euler decomposition holds in factor coordinates; Theorem 2 gives the volatility risk contribution of factor j as (A'x)_j (A+ Sigma x)_j / sigma(x); budgets set on assets can leave factor risk unbalanced (7 equity + 3 bond indices -> equity is 70% of ERC risk).
impact_on_spec: TRS = Euler contribution of the orthogonalised SMH factor to sleeve variance is the capped quantity.
independent_replication: Standard result (Euler allocation; also Menchero-Davis x-sigma-rho); not an empirical claim.
limitations: Theory; no semiconductor or cost evidence.
quote: if the universe includes 7 equity indices and 3 bond indices, the equity risk of the ERC portfolio represents then 70% of the portfolio’s total risk, a solution very unbalanced between equity and bond risks.

claim: MSCI Barra USE4 models equity returns with industry and style factors plus specific risk; industry exposure is risk in the factor covariance, not a forecast.
impact_on_spec: A theme is managed as a factor risk unit with a budget; motivates the cap rather than cycle timing.
independent_replication: Industry practice (also BlackRock fundamental model per T-81, search summary only).
limitations: Methodology note; the quoted line describes the factor structure lineage.
quote: using countries, industries, and styles as explanatory factors, as described by Grinold, Rudd, and Stefek

claim: Stanford and BlackRock authors: commercial risk models may miss changing regimes and transient factors; adding transient statistical factors captures the missed structure.
impact_on_spec: Use a dedicated rolling theme factor (126 sessions) rather than a static industry map.
limitations: Preprint; statistical factors, not a named ETF theme.
quote: while these models are typically of high quality, they may fail to capture important information, e.g., changing market regimes and transient factors.

claim: MSCI stress-tests thematic indexes with its crowding model and scenarios; crowding helped explain the efficient-energy theme's 2021 underperformance.
impact_on_spec: Benefit is measured with theme-shock replays and stress-window ES, not only full-sample Sharpe.
quote: Crowding in the efficient-energy theme rose throughout 2020 and stayed moderately high through Q1 2021. Its underperformance since March can be explained, in part, by its crowding characteristics.

claim: Alpaca: 50% initial margin; overnight maintenance 30% long above $6, 50% long 2x leveraged ETF, 75% long 3x leveraged ETF, short >= $5 greater of $5/share or 30%; $0 borrow fees on easy-to-borrow shares; margin interest 6.50% for non-elite users.
impact_on_spec: H1 feasibility rules, 0 bp main borrow, 6.5% debit and re-levering cost.

claim: Hsieh et al.: leveraged ETF performance depends on return autocorrelation and dynamics, not only volatility drag.
impact_on_spec: The cash-account hedge is evaluated with actual SOXS returns (path-dependent decay), never -3 x SMH.
independent_replication: Consistent with standard LETF compounding algebra.
quote: We show that this view is incomplete: LETF performance depends fundamentally on return autocorrelation and return dynamics.

claim: SOX lost about 21% in July 2026 (worst month since October 2008) while the S&P 500 total return slipped 0.1%; attributed to crowding and leverage.
impact_on_spec: Defines replay R3; theme risk materialised without a fundamental turn.
independent_replication: SMH 06-30..07-29 655.9 -> 504.2 per plan v2 3.2 (to be recomputed from SIP in build.json).
limitations: Practitioner commentary; BofA survey figures second-hand.
quote: The PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index (SOX) lost about 21% in July, its worst monthly performance since October 2008. By contrast, the S&P 500 Total Return Index slipped just 0.1%, underscoring how narrowly the market damage was concentrated.
